First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.
